extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians (number theory/arithmetic geometry) evaluating or responding to critiques of IUTch
extracted.subtask_description: A point-by-point expert rebuttal to a manuscript criticizing Inter‑universal Teichmüller Theory (IUTch). The rubric covers what a valid critique must include (definitions, identifications, proofs, and linkages to core IUTch notions) and what constitutes misrepresentation or inessential simplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link criticisms precisely to IUTch notation/terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: If one asserts results about the validity or invalidity of IUTch, the discussion must be tightly linked, at the level of notation, terminology, and precise references, to the theory developed in [IUTchI]–[IUTchIV]; omissions of key notions (e.g., “multiradial”, “log-shell”, “tensor-packet”, “procession”, indeterminacies “(Ind1,2,3)”) render the critique incomplete or misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript [SS2018-05] makes strong assertions concerning IUTch while only partially linking notation/terminology to the original theory; a rigorous critique should explicitly reference and discuss the central notions and how they are being used or misused (cf. C1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat simplifications as globally inessential
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a specific simplification results in 'an essential obfuscation of the ideas' depends on which aspect of the ideas is under discussion; a simplification may be harmless for some aspects but fatal for others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must analyze which aspects are affected by a simplification rather than asserting a blanket non-essentiality; Mochizuki notes SS's blanket claim is not justified and that their own understanding of deeper parts was limited (cf. C2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify any aggressive identifications/simplifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplifications such as identifying the choice of a Hodge theater with the choice of an abstractly isomorphic curve, or identifying identical objects along the identity, are not automatically inessential and must be justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such identifications can destroy essential structure; the author must give detailed explanations or references (Mochizuki attempted to explain during discussions; see Rpt2018) rather than asserting they are harmless (cf. C3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid blanket statements as substitutes for proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that 'even with all subtleties restored, the issue we are pointing out will prevail' do not constitute rigorous proofs or even sketches of proofs of central assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid critique must provide rigorous arguments or sketches, not sweeping assertions that rest on misunderstandings (cf. C4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the role of anabelian geometry explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: If denying the necessity of anabelian geometry in IUTch, one must confront the structural role of étale-like objects (Galois groups/arithmetic fundamental groups) and explain or construct any claimed automorphisms or proofs of non-existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SS should either construct explicit automorphisms of the log-theta-lattice (permuting 0- and 1-columns) or give explicit proofs of non-existence; vague appeals to general anabelian results are insufficient (see Q1, Q2 and C5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not identify domain and codomain of the log-link without proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying the domain and codomain of the log-link is not harmless: it forces identification of Θ-links which depend essentially on multiplicative structures and chosen basepoints; such identifications are generally incompatible with the Θ-link definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claim of invariance under identifying domain/codomain must be supported by a rigorous proof/sketch; asking for a proof of invariance of the Θ-link under such identifications is natural (see Q3 and C6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect Π-equivariance and Frobenius-like data when rigidifying Π’s
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigidifying arithmetic fundamental groups Π by fixed rigidifying isomorphisms (rather than allowing poly-isomorphisms) affects essential content because these rigidifications depend on Π-actions on local rings/fields and Frobenius-like (0-column) data that do not admit switching symmetries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one claims such rigidifications are harmless, one must show how the necessary Frobenius-like data and Π-actions are preserved; otherwise the correct description is collections of isomorphic topological groups related only by poly-isomorphisms (cf. C7).

rubrics_metrics.name: State conditions for canonical/unique determination of γ-elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements such as γv and γcan exist for a global realified Frobenioid but are not uniquely or canonically determined unless the Frobenioid is given as part of an F×μ-prime-strip context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must state when uniqueness holds and reference constructions (e.g., factorization of the forgetful functor) that produce canonical determination; failure to state this leads to incorrect claims of canonicity (cf. C8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use correct local generator conventions and group labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Local generators of the value group in the discussed context are obtained from the unique generator of the (Frobenius-like) monoid; étale-like data such as Gv cannot be related to non-divisible Frobenius-like value groups by Kummer theory, and notation like 'Z' must be replaced by the correct profinite variant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor technical corrections (e.g., replace 'Z' by '̂Z' or the appropriate profinite notation) are necessary to avoid inaccurate statements about relationships between Gv and value groups (cf. C9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Range v only over bad primes in pilot-object definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the definition of 'pilot objects', the index v should run only over the bad primes (Vbad) relevant to the construction, not over all primes of the number field; also certain valuations should include multiplicative factors (v(q)→v(q)·γv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful indexing and correct valuation formulas are essential even if they are 'inessential technical errors' in form; they affect correct formulation of pilot objects (cf. C10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish the isomorphism sending γcan→1 from arithmetic degree in general
rubrics_metrics.description: The isomorphism that maps γcan→1 need not coincide with the arithmetic degree in general; it does coincide for q-pilot objects but not for Θ-pilot objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not conflate these notions and must indicate the contexts where coincidences occur (cf. C11, C12, C14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret 'j^2' correctly in averages/expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Occurrences of 'j^2' in certain formulas likely refer to the average of the j^2 for j = 1, …, l, not a single index squared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether averages are intended to avoid misstatements in arithmetic-degree-type computations (cf. C13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure Θ-pilot objects' arithmetic-degree identification is properly scaled
rubrics_metrics.description: For Θ-pilot objects, the identification to the arithmetic-degree involves scaling by the average of the j^2; this differs from the q-pilot case and must be stated correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state scaling factors when identifying isomorphisms with arithmetic degree in the Θ-case (cf. C14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical choices for the Θ-link must permit multiradial algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: A purported 'canonical choice for the Θ-link' must satisfy the conditions necessary to apply the multiradial algorithms of IUTch; certain 'id-versions' fail these conditions and are not usable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before declaring a canonical Θ-link, verify the multiradial applicability conditions (cf. C15 and [Rpt2018], §10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish abstract pilot objects from their multiradial concrete representations
rubrics_metrics.description: One must properly distinguish abstract category-theoretic pilot objects (determined by intrinsic structure of prime-strips) from their concrete multiradial representations on tensor-packets of log-shells; conflating them is a major source of misunderstanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction is central to IUTch (see [IUTchIII], Theorem 3.11); omission of tensor-packets/log-shells in a critique indicates a substantive gap (cf. C16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not introduce erroneous identifications or commuting loops in proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof of [IUTchIII], Corollary 3.12 does not require 'careful identifications of copies of real numbers', 'consistently identifying' copies, introducing a commuting 'loop', or inserting scalars; such features arise only from erroneous identifications of labels/ring structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing the proof, avoid modifications that arbitrarily identify distinct labels/ring structures (N1–N5); these modifications create spurious contradictions absent from the genuine argument (cf. C17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate superficial contradictions from genuine logical gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Superficial internal contradictions obtained by arbitrarily modifying/identifying distinct objects in an argument are fundamentally different from genuine gaps or flaws in the logical structure of the original argument; criticisms must show flaws in the actual theory, not in a modified, erroneously identified version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A correct critique should engage the actual multiradial representation and logical structure of IUTch rather than a superficially altered variant (cf. C18 and references to [Rpt2018]).
